title: Gelatin: what it means for your plan
standfirst: Which of our plan rules this ingredient turns on, and what that does not tell you.

spans.text: Gelatin is a protein set into a gel, made by boiling animal skin, bones, and connective tissue (usually pork or beef). It gives foods a jelly-like texture.
Why it is in your food
Manufacturers use gelatin as a gelling agent and it is of animal origin.
Our rules read gelatin as meat or fish.

Our scorer looks for gelatin when Halal, Kosher, Pregnancy, Vegan or Vegetarian is on for you. If those plans are off, your score does not change. This is how the app reads a label. It is not a claim about health.
Labels do not all use the same word for this. Below is every spelling we watch for. Some come from other languages, because a pack made for another country prints its own.
One word on a label can cover more than one thing. A plan may also turn on how much is in the food, which this page cannot see. Read the pack when it matters.
